title: Prosecutors Examined Firm With Tie to Judge in Trump Hush Money Trial
partialText: The U.S. attorney in Chicago subpoenaed a fund-raising firm that had been co-owned by the daughter of Judge Juan Merchan, who conducted the trial that led to Donald Trump’s felony conviction.

title: How Cyclospora Evaded the U.S. Food Safety System to Sicken Thousands
partialText: The Trump administration delayed a rule last year that could have sped up the effort to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Critics charge that food safety oversight has eroded overall.

title: Navy and USS Lincoln’s Problems Are Tied to Attacks on U.S. Base Early in War
partialText: Diego Garcia, a tiny island 2,200 miles from the Gulf of Oman, took over as the Navy’s logistics hub after Iran damaged a base in Bahrain.

title: Canadian Petition to Expel U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra Takes Off
partialText: Mr. Hoekstra has been President Trump’s faithful messenger in Canada amid a historic low in relations. More than 170,000 Canadians want him gone.

title: As China Pushes to Expand in Asia, Trump Focuses on Iran
partialText: Asian allies are beginning to wonder whether the United States would or could defend them in a war.

title: The Iranian YouTube Show Posing Questions Few Dare Ask
partialText: Azad, a popular online debate program, has tackled topics that push the limits of Iran’s authoritarian system. Some question how it has remained on air.

title: Israeli Strikes in Lebanon Kill 11, Health Officials Say
partialText: The Lebanese health ministry said several children were killed in a strike overnight, one of the deadliest attacks in months. Israel’s military said it was targeting Hezbollah infrastructure.

title: Iran Says Qatar Captured Three of Its Pilots Early in War With U.S.
partialText: Iran said the airmen have been held since March 2 when their fighter jets were shot down. The Qatari government has not commented.

title: Professor’s Death Leaves Behind Hard Questions for Cambridge on Race and Hiring
partialText: Jason Arday, the school’s youngest Black professor, was found dead on Friday. The school ignored a series of warnings about his life story and his work.

title: Sherrod Brown Seeks Senate Comeback in Ohio, Hoping His Populist Pitch Still Resonates
partialText: At 73, Sherrod Brown is mounting a comeback bid in Ohio. He is one of the Democrats his party is counting on to retake control of the Senate.

title: Can Senator Ed Markey’s Progressive Politics Help Him Overcome the Age Issue?
partialText: Ed Markey is hoping that his progressive politics will save him in Massachusetts.

title: Heat Deaths in a ‘Cold’ Country Are a Warning to the Rest of Europe
partialText: A June heat wave in Belgium and neighboring countries exposed a lethal lack of readiness. That’s a risk as another wave hits Europe.

title: The Charming, Amusing, Surprisingly Low-Confidence Matthew Rhys
partialText: The “Widow’s Bay” star on his two Emmy nominations, his penchant for going dark and his wobbly self-esteem.

title: Republicans Are Trying to Hide These Health Care Cuts
partialText: Republicans are taking deliberate steps to make health care less affordable.

title: David Ellison’s Plan to Move Hollywood to Nashville
partialText: The dream of a red-state Hollywood.

title: Quit Lit
partialText: There are good reasons to abandon books we’re not enjoying, but our attenuated attention might lead us to tap out too early.

title: At Least 47 Dead as 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake Rocks Indonesia
partialText: The temblor was one of the strongest the area had experienced in decades, an official said.
